title: Geopolitical Daily
preheader: The government suspended the court's chief, prompting protests and coup accusations.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Saturday, October 31, 2026 — the 2 stories that matter most today, plus 3 updates on stories you're following and 6 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Poland suspends constitutional court chief and deploys riot police
stories.why_important: Poland's government suspended the head of the Constitutional Tribunal, and police sealed the building, prompting protests and coup accusations. The clash between Prime Minister Donald Tusk and conservative opponents over judicial control could reshape how the EU treats Warsaw. It could also test the rule of law in a key NATO state.
stories.what_overlooked: Police detained protesters, The Hindu reports, a detail missing from most early accounts.
stories.prediction: Poland's parliament or president will respond to the suspension; a formal court challenge would show whether the government can make the move stick.

stories.story_title: US approves possible sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
stories.why_important: The State Department approved a possible $2.1 billion sale of 500 PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine, funded by allies and EU loans. It answers Kyiv's complaints about shrinking air defenses, but Congress must review it and deliveries could take years.
stories.what_overlooked: Ukraine's president warned deliveries could take years, and international partners and EU loans, not US money, fully fund the sale.
stories.prediction: Congress will schedule a review of the missile sale; a formal objection from lawmakers would show whether the deal can proceed quickly.

quick_hits.text: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia's last independent newspapers, said it is closing after years of Kremlin pressure and the eviction of its Moscow office.
France banned city-center protests and warned of Halloween violence as it braced for a third weekend of youth-led demonstrations over prices and prospects.
The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi drone over the Mecca region; the Houthis denied launching any attack toward Saudi Arabia.
US, South Korean and Japanese officials vowed to complete North Korea's denuclearisation, ahead of speculation about a Trump-Kim meeting at APEC.
Pope Leo XIV became the first pontiff to vote in a US election, submitting a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of the November 3 midterms.
Trump said the Iran war will 'get wrapped up soon' while Iran said it is ready to answer any attack.

views.framing: Frames a rule-of-law battle caused by Tusk’s suspension of a nationalist-linked court chief, stressing coup accusations and clashes.
views.quote: A bid to remove the court’s nationalist-linked leadership sparked accusations of a coup and clashes between protesters and police in Warsaw.

views.framing: Stresses Tusk government’s push to remove right-wing-appointed judges, linking unrest to next year’s election.
views.quote: Poland PM Donald Tusk's government has been trying to force out the top court's judges, who were appointed by the previous right-wing government.

views.framing: Frames a pro-European government versus conservative opponents over judicial independence, highlighting the president joining protesters.
views.quote: Poland’s president has cut short a trip to Senegal, joining protesters facing off with police.

views.framing: Casts the crisis as a power struggle between rival judges over control of the Constitutional Tribunal, prompting police deployment.
views.quote: Police deployed outside Poland's top court as rival groups of judges dispute who controls institution

views.framing: Presents the court’s coup accusation against Tusk and blocked presidential access as the central confrontation.
views.quote: Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal has accused Prime Minister Donald Tusk of waging a judicial “coup d’etat”

views.framing: Frames the suspension as an escalating judicial standoff between Tusk and the opposition, citing AP.
views.quote: Poland’s constitutional court chief suspended amid escalating judicial standoff between Prime Minister Donald Tusk and the opposition

perspective_grid.blindspot: G20 foreign ministers opened talks in the United States, with sharp disagreements over the Ukraine and Iran wars splitting members. The rift matters globally because it complicates coordinated action on sanctions, energy and security.

developing.text: Investigators link North Korean hackers to $6.3bn Binance theft.
Russia offered floating nuclear power plants to coastal African countries at the Russia-Africa summit, a push to expand its nuclear business on the continent.
Uganda asked the African Union to send medical and logistical staff to help Congo's Ebola outbreak, which has now killed more than 5,000 people.
